name: Duchy of Berry
alt: Duchy of Berry (John of Berry's apanage)

predecessors.name: Royal domain of France
predecessors.text: 'On October 1360, King John II created the peerage-duchy of Berry as an appanage for his third-born son'; Auvergne with it

successors.name: Royal domain of France
successors.text: Berry passes to Dauphin John and then Dauphin Charles (Duchy of Berry page) and 'returned to the royal domain' with Charles VII; Poitou 'merged into the royal domain' (infobox of the John page)

successors.name: House of Bourbon
successors.text: Marie 'succeeded him as Duchess of Auvergne'

rulers.name: John, Duke of Berry (John of Poitiers)

ledger.x: October 1360: King John II creates the duchy of Berry as an appanage for his third son John of Poitiers.
1360: Auvergne is raised to a duchy for John with Berry.
1378: the French reconquer the lands lost at Brétigny, among them Poitou, of which John was count.
15 June 1416: John of Berry dies and Poitou merges into the royal domain.
1416: Auvergne goes to John's daughter Marie.
1416: Berry passes to John's grandnephew Dauphin John and, in 1417, to Dauphin Charles.
June 1416: the composite lands of John of Berry are dispersed: Berry to the Dauphins, Poitou to the domain, Auvergne to Marie.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War (reconquest of Poitou)
wars.outcome: Charles V's reconquest regained most of the Brétigny lands by 1378, among them Poitou, where John of Berry was count.

certainty.note: An apanage with no boundary record on the pages.
